page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-144 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 144 vCPUs and 1116 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 72 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled (2.0 threads per core). The dedicated CPU operates at a base speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a 504 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core CPU performance in stress-ng is in the average tier, multi-core CPU performance ranks in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 11561.41 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 533.18 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% tier. The instance also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in cryptographic operations, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression. For LLM workloads, prompt processing speeds consistently rank in the top 10% tier across small, medium, and large models, though text generation for smaller models drops to the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-144 offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with massive multi-threaded compute power. This makes it suitable for memory-intensive and highly parallelized workloads such as large-scale database operations, software compilation, and LLM prompt processing. However, the lack of local storage requires external block storage attachments, which should be factored into the overall architectural design.
